p: The selected four-group phase schedule completes all 34 feasible batch/context cells, with six configured-capacity skips, as do target-only, standard EAGLE3, and the previous overlap schedule. This is 136 measured workloads in the four columns below. Native TBO-on cases b and d remain unsupported startup configurations across their 40 cells each; they are not included as measured performance results.

Standard EAGLE3 / target-only throughput has geometric mean 0.807× over 34 cells (range 0.680–0.931×); every measured cell is slower with speculation on this synthetic workload. The selected phase / previous schedule ratio has geometric mean 0.972× over the 29 split-batch cells (range 0.951–1.003×; 1/29 cell medians exceed 1.0×). Batch 1 follows ordinary EAGLE3 and is excluded from scheduling-gain aggregates.

All 4,371 timed token sequences in the selected schedule’s 34 workloads exactly match the previous schedule’s same-prompt reference output. This verifies the change between those schedules; comparisons with unmodified EAGLE3 and target-only decoding are reported separately below.

Capacity-limited cells are B256/32k; B128 and B256/64k; and B64, B128, and B256/128k. The resident token allowance is about 7.23 million for target-only and 6.65 million with the draft. These skips describe this memory configuration, not universal model limits. At 128k every mode uses 130,938 prompt tokens plus 128 output tokens, retaining six boundary slots.

Throughput is the median of three unprofiled cached-prefix request waves. Server runs were sequential, not randomized; small percentage differences may include run-to-run drift and are not confidence intervals. Full minimum/maximum ranges, cold latency, acceptance, output validation, and per-rank profiled GPU activity spans are retained in the CSV/JSON. Profiled iteration span includes nested launches and gaps between them; it is not kernel busy time or an unprofiled latency estimate.
